## Part A — Classification working (analytical core)

### A.0 Inputs, method, and the governing rule

**Composition (as supplied):**

| Component | CAS | EC | Conc. | Component harmonised classification (CLP Annex VI) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2-Butoxyethanol (2-BE) | 111-76-2 | 203-905-0 | 15 % | Acute Tox. 4 (oral/dermal/inhalation); Skin Irrit. 2; Eye Irrit. 2 — **[VERIFY exact Annex VI entry, Index No., ATP & any SCL against the licensed Annex VI text]** |
| Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) | 1310-73-2 | 215-185-5 | 5 % | Skin Corr. 1A (H314), with specific concentration limits (SCLs) — **[VERIFY exact Annex VI entry, Index No. & SCLs]** |
| Water | 7732-18-5 | 231-791-2 | to balance (~80 %) | Not classified |

**Data held:** physico-chemical (pH 13.2; non-flammable); in-vitro skin corrosion/irritation study (on the mixture); serious eye damage study (on the mixture); acute oral toxicity study (LD50 held for 2-BE — *value not supplied to this draft*).
**Data NOT held:** skin/respiratory sensitisation; CMR (C, M, R); STOT-RE; aspiration; aquatic-environmental (no study).

**Governing method & citations (structural references — verify exact clause against the licensed text):**
- **CLP Article 4 & 5** — classification duty; the **Annex VI harmonised classification of each component is binding** and takes precedence over self-classification for the endpoints it covers. Self-classification fills only the gaps.
- **CLP Article 9** — permitted methods: test data on the mixture → bridging principles → the **calculation/summation method**.
- **Mixture route used here:** where a **mixture test result** exists (skin, eye), it governs that endpoint; where it does not (acute tox), the **calculation/summation (additivity) method** is applied from the known composition — **CLP Annex I Part 3** (§3.1 acute tox / ATE additivity §3.1.3.6; §3.2 skin corrosion/irritation additivity §3.2.3; §3.3 eye §3.3.3).
- **[VERIFY]** Governing rule of this skill: the binding numeric concentration limits, SCLs and ATE conversion values below are **not reconstructed as authoritative from memory** — each is flagged **[VERIFY]** and must be read from the licensed CLP Annex I / Annex VI before finalisation. The arithmetic is shown transparently so a competent person can re-run it.

### A.1 Physical hazards

| Class | Determination | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Flammability (liquid) | **Not classified** | Physico-chemical data held: **non-flammable**; aqueous (~80 % water). Determined on held data. |
| **Corrosive to metals** (CLP §2.16) | **[GAP] — NOT classified** | pH 13.2 (alkaline) suggests possible metal reactivity, **but the class requires the specific corrosion-rate-on-metal test (steel/aluminium)** — no such test is held. Route to testing; do not classify on pH alone. |
| Explosives, oxidising, gases under pressure, self-reactive, pyrophoric, self-heating, organic peroxides | **Not applicable** | **[ASSUMPTION]** — no oxidising, explosophoric, self-reactive or peroxide-forming groups in the stated composition (aqueous NaOH / glycol ether). Confirm no such component is present in the full formulation. |

### A.2 Skin corrosion/irritation — **Skin Corr. 1, H314**

**Classified.** Three independent lines of the stated data converge (the classification is over-determined):

1. **Mixture test data (primary):** an in-vitro skin corrosion/irritation study is held on the mixture → governs the endpoint under CLP Art. 9 (mixture test data ranks above calculation).
2. **Summation / additivity route (CLP Annex I §3.2.3):** NaOH is Annex VI **Skin Corr. 1A** and is present at **5 %**. NaOH's Annex VI **specific concentration limits (SCLs)** place a Skin Corr. 1A contribution at **C ≥ 5 %** **[VERIFY SCL values]** → at 5 % NaOH the mixture reaches **Skin Corr. 1** by the additivity method on this ingredient alone.
3. **pH extreme:** pH **13.2 ≥ 11.5** independently supports Skin Corr. 1 (subject to acid/alkali-reserve consideration) **[VERIFY the pH/reserve criterion]**.

> **Sub-category (1A / 1B / 1C):** **1A is *indicated*** by the 5 % NaOH Annex VI SCL and pH 13.2 — but the sub-category is properly set by the **held in-vitro study readout**, whose category outcome was **not supplied to this draft**. **[GAP]** — confirm the sub-category from the in-vitro study report and the alkali-reserve result. (The label carries H314 regardless of sub-category, so this gap does not block labelling.)

### A.3 Serious eye damage/irritation — **Eye Dam. 1, H318**

**Classified.** Two lines converge:
1. **Mixture test data:** a serious eye damage study is held on the mixture.
2. **Consequential rule (CLP Annex I §3.3):** a mixture classified **Skin Corr. 1** is **also** classified **Eye Dam. 1** — no separate eye test is even required. **[VERIFY the consequential rule]**.

> **Label interaction:** where **H314** applies, **H318 is not stated separately on the label** (H314 already covers serious eye damage); the single **GHS05** pictogram serves both. H318 is retained in the *classification* record (§2) for completeness.

### A.4 Acute toxicity — assessed by ATE additivity; provisionally NOT classified

**Method:** ATE additivity, **CLP Annex I §3.1.3.6.1** — `100 / ATEmix = Σ (Cᵢ / ATEᵢ)`.
**Relevant contributor:** only **2-BE (15 %)** carries a harmonised acute-tox classification (Acute Tox. 4). **NaOH carries no harmonised acute-tox classification** (Skin Corr. 1A only) → it is **not** an acute-tox contributor. Composition is fully known (water balance), so the "unknown ingredients" adjustment (§3.1.3.6.2.2) does not apply.

**Oral (worked transparently):**
- Using the **CLP Table 3.1.2 conversion value for Acute Tox. 4 (oral) = 500 mg/kg** **[VERIFY]** as a stand-in for the un-supplied real LD50:
  `100 / ATEmix = 15 / 500 = 0.030` → **ATEmix ≈ 3 333 mg/kg**.
- This sits **above the Acute Tox. 4 oral upper bound (2 000 mg/kg)** **[VERIFY band]** → the mixture is **NOT classified for acute oral toxicity** on the calculation.
- **[GAP]** The **actual held 2-BE oral LD50 was not supplied to this draft.** The competent person must substitute the real LD50 and re-run. 2-BE's harmonised Cat 4 implies an LD50 in the 300–2 000 mg/kg range, so the "not classified" outcome is *likely* robust at 15 % — but it must be confirmed with the real value, not the conversion default.

**Dermal & inhalation:** **[GAP] — not evaluated in this draft.** 2-BE is Annex VI Acute Tox. 4 by both routes; the same additivity applies. **Inhalation is method-sensitive** — if the concentrate is **applied by spray/mist**, the mist ATE conversion value is far lower than the vapour value and could change the outcome. Route to the competent person with the intended application method specified.

### A.5 2-BE component irritation — subsumed

2-BE is Annex VI **Skin Irrit. 2 / Eye Irrit. 2**. Both are **subsumed** by the mixture's more severe **Skin Corr. 1 / Eye Dam. 1** — no separate lower classification is carried (the higher category governs).

| STOT-repeated exposure | **[GAP]** no data — note 2-BE's recognised **haemolytic/haematological** effects warrant explicit STOT-RE/blood evaluation | Competent person — registration dossier + literature |

**Precautionary statements (codes + intent — competent person confirms wording, and prunes to the most relevant; CLP guidance: normally ≤ 6 P-statements on a label unless severity requires more):**
- **Prevention:** P260 (do not breathe mist/vapour/spray) · P264 (wash skin thoroughly after handling) · P280 (wear protective gloves / clothing / eye + face protection).
- **Response (highest priority for a corrosive):** P301+P330+P331 (IF SWALLOWED: rinse mouth; do NOT induce vomiting) · P303+P361+P353 (IF ON SKIN/hair: remove contaminated clothing immediately; rinse skin/shower) · P305+P351+P338 (IF IN EYES: rinse cautiously several minutes; remove contact lenses if easy; continue rinsing) · P304+P340 (IF INHALED: fresh air, keep comfortable for breathing) · **P310 (immediately call a POISON CENTER/doctor)** · P363 (wash contaminated clothing before reuse).
- **Storage/Disposal:** P405 (store locked up) · P501 (dispose per local/national regulation).

**Supplier identity block:** name / full address / telephone **[GAP — not supplied]**.
**Packaging safety features:** Child-resistant fastening (CRF) and tactile warning of danger (TWD) are triggered by H314 **for supply to the general public only**. As this is **industrial/professional-only** supply, CRF/TWD are **not required** on that basis — **[VERIFY** the exact CLP Art. 35 / Annex II §3.1 trigger and confirm the product is never made available to consumers].

**Label ⇄ classification consistency check (SME lens):** Danger + Category 1 + GHS05 + H314 are mutually consistent; the single most-severe pictogram rule is respected; H318 correctly omitted under H314. ✔

## Part C — 16-section Safety Data Sheet (DRAFT)

### Section 1 — Identification
- **Product identifier:** Industrial Alkaline Hard-Surface Cleaner (concentrate) **[ASSUMPTION — trade name not supplied → GAP]**.
- **Relevant identified uses:** industrial / professional **hard-surface cleaning**. **Uses advised against:** consumer/domestic use; any use generating uncontrolled spray/mist without exposure controls (see §8).
- **Supplier:** name / address / e-mail of the competent person responsible for the SDS **[GAP — not supplied]**.
- **Emergency telephone:** 24-h emergency number / national poison centre **[GAP — not supplied]**.

### Section 2 — Hazard identification
- **Classification (CLP):** **Skin Corr. 1, H314**; **Eye Dam. 1, H318** *(H318 subsumed by H314 on the label)*. Acute toxicity provisionally **not classified** (see §A.4, **[GAP]**).
- **Label elements:** GHS05 · **Danger** · **H314** · P-statements per Part B.
- **Other hazards:** highly alkaline (**pH 13.2**). **PBT/vPvB:** **[GAP]** — not assessed; requires the REACH registration data. **Endocrine-disruptor properties:** **[GAP]** — not assessed.

### Section 3 — Composition / information on ingredients
Mixture. Hazardous components disclosed per §A.0 table (2-BE 15 %, CAS 111-76-2 / EC 203-905-0; NaOH 5 %, CAS 1310-73-2 / EC 215-185-5; water to balance). REACH registration numbers of the components **[GAP — not supplied; insert from the registration dossiers]**. Full component classifications are the Annex VI harmonised entries **[VERIFY]**.

### Section 4 — First-aid measures
- **Eyes (highest priority):** rinse immediately and continuously with water for at least 15 minutes, holding eyelids open; remove contact lenses if easy; **seek immediate medical/ophthalmological attention** (risk of serious eye damage). *(Exact protocol to be confirmed by an occupational health professional.)*
- **Skin:** remove contaminated clothing immediately; wash/shower with copious water; do not rub; seek medical attention for chemical burns.
- **Ingestion:** rinse mouth; **do NOT induce vomiting** (corrosive); give water to drink if conscious; **immediate medical attention / poison centre**.
- **Inhalation (mist/vapour):** move to fresh air; keep comfortable for breathing; medical attention if symptoms persist.
- **Notes to physician:** corrosive alkaline burn; contains 2-BE — **[GAP]** flag potential haematological monitoring consideration for a competent occupational physician to evaluate. Detailed first-aid text to be finalised by a competent person.

### Section 5 — Fire-fighting measures
- Product is **non-flammable** (held data). Use extinguishing media appropriate to the surrounding fire. **Hazardous combustion/decomposition products [GAP]** — not characterised; assume irritant/corrosive vapours possible on involvement in fire. Full-face self-contained breathing apparatus for firefighters (standard). Contain firewater run-off (alkaline). *(Detail for competent-person completion.)*

### Section 6 — Accidental release measures
- **Personal precautions:** corrosive — see §8 controls; keep unprotected personnel away; ventilate; avoid generating mist.
- **Environmental precautions:** prevent entry to drains/watercourses (alkaline; **aquatic hazard [GAP] — not classified**, so precautionary containment applies pending the ecotox assessment).
- **Clean-up:** contain and absorb with inert non-combustible absorbent; neutralise residues cautiously per a validated method **[VERIFY method]**; collect for disposal (§13).

### Section 7 — Handling and storage
- **Handling:** industrial/professional users only; avoid skin/eye contact and mist inhalation; do not decant into unlabelled containers; provide eyewash/safety shower at point of use (see §8).
- **Storage:** store locked up, upright, closed; segregate from **acids** (violent neutralisation), **oxidisers**, and reactive metals (alkali/metal reaction — H₂ evolution potential; ties to the **corrosive-to-metals [GAP]**). Compatible container materials **[VERIFY]** (avoid aluminium/zinc/tin — attacked by alkali). Keep away from foodstuffs.

### Section 8 — Exposure controls / personal protection — **hierarchy-of-controls-first**

**Occupational exposure limits (source + year):**

| Agent | Limit | Source · year | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2-Butoxyethanol | 8-h TWA **20 ppm (98 mg/m³)**; STEL **50 ppm (246 mg/m³)**; **"skin"** notation | **EU Indicative OELV — Directive 2000/39/EC (2000)** | **[VERIFY exact values & currency** against the consolidated Chemical Agents Directive 98/24/EC indicative-OEL lists / latest ATP; national OELs may be stricter] |
| Sodium hydroxide | **No EU-wide indicative OEL** | — | **[GAP]** — several Member States apply a **ceiling** value (order of ~2 mg/m³); the **occupational hygienist (role)** must resolve the applicable **national** OEL for the site of use |
| Water | None | — | — |

**DNEL / PNEC:** **[GAP]** — take 2-BE DNELs (worker, inhalation/dermal) and PNECs from the REACH registration dossier / component (e)SDS; not supplied to this draft.

**Controls — ranked, most effective first (KB-SNIP-HOC):**

| Level | Control (named to the hazard) |
|---|---|
| **Elimination** | Where the cleaning outcome allows, **remove manual handling of the corrosive concentrate** — deliver via a fixed, plumbed **closed dosing/dilution system** so operators never contact the neat product (eliminates the concentrate-contact hazard at the task). |
| **Substitution** | Evaluate a **less hazardous cleaning chemistry** or a **lower-alkalinity / pre-diluted formulation** that achieves the same result at a pH/NaOH content that drops the mixture out of Skin Corr. 1 — a formulation decision for the competent person. |
| **Engineering** | **Automated dilution/dosing** and **closed transfer** (no open decanting); **local exhaust ventilation (LEV)** at any point that generates mist/spray or vapour; **splash screens/guarding** at wash stations; **plumbed emergency eyewash + safety shower** within the required reach of every use point; bunded storage. |
| **Administrative** | Restrict to **trained, authorised industrial users**; safe system of work / SOP for dosing, decanting-prohibition and spill response; **no consumer supply**; signage at use/storage points; supervision; health-surveillance referral where the competent occupational physician requires it (links to the STOT-RE **[GAP]**). |
| **PPE — last line only** | Chemical-resistant gloves (**nitrile or butyl — confirm breakthrough time for 2-BE + 5 % NaOH; [VERIFY glove material/EN 374]**); **eye + face protection** (chemical goggles + face shield for splash tasks); chemical-resistant apron/coverall and boots for splash-risk tasks; **RPE only where mist/vapour monitoring shows airborne levels approach the 2-BE OEL despite LEV** — RPE is not a substitute for the engineering controls above. |

> **HoC note:** PPE is presented **last** and only as the final barrier behind elimination/substitution/engineering — never as the primary treatment. Any residual reliance on administrative/PPE controls (e.g. where a closed dosing system is not yet installed) must be **justified as not-reasonably-practicable-otherwise, or escalated** for engineering investment. (See action A-4.)

SME review **ran** in this context (two lenses per this skill's persona set): **Industrial toxicologist / GHS-CLP classification SME** — every assigned class (Skin Corr. 1, Eye Dam. 1) is forced by the stated mixture data via the cited method; every absent datum is honestly **[GAP]**, none back-filled; the calculation/summation method and its limits are stated. **Regulatory-affairs / SDS-format specialist** — the 16-section set + CLP label match the resolved **EU (CLP+REACH)** regime; the ≥10 t CSR/e-SDS duty and §14 hand-off are surfaced; §8 is HoC-ranked (PPE last). Universal gates checked: no de-identification leak (owners are role labels); no invented class/threshold/citation (numeric limits flagged **[VERIFY]**); no PPE-only treatment presented as complete; every action owned and dated.

**This is decision-support only. It PRECEDES — and does not replace or constitute — the human competent-person sign-off. It does not certify the SDS as "approved by a competent person."** Release for use only after Action A-7 closes.
